Ang Liu1,∗Zhi-Long Han2,† and Fei Huang2,3‡


1School of Physical Science and Electronic Engineering, Jining University, Shandong 273155, China


2School of Physics and Technology, University of Jinan, Jinan, Shandong 250022, China and


3State Key Laboratory of Dark Matter Physics, School of Physics and Astronomy,


Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai 200240, China


(Dated: July 10, 2026)


In the conventional Z′ portal dark matter scenario, the prediction of detectable dark matter χ


typically relies on the collider sensitivities of Z′ and direct detection, where the Majorana type right-


handed neutrinos are usually assumed. However, if the right-handed neutrinos νR are Dirac type,


they will contribute to the additional effective number of relativistic species ∆Neff, which brings


different detectable predictions for Z′ portal dark matter. In light of the great improvement of ∆Neff


for the upcoming experiments, we investigate the Z′ portal dark matter with Dirac type νR. Under the


U(1)B−L symmetry, this model includes νR with U(1)B−L charge QνR = −1 and χ with arbitrary


Qχ beyond the SM. Based on the relation in the production of χ and νR, both the WIMP and FIMP


dark matter through the Z′ portal scenario are considered. We perform a comprehensive exploration


of the viable parameter space under the constraints from ∆Neff induced by thermal and non-thermal


νR, perturbative limit, dark matter direct and indirect detection, and collider searches of Z′.


arXiv:2607.08082v1  [hep-ph]  9 Jul 2026


∗AL@jnxy.edu.cn


† sps hanzl@ujn.edu.cn


‡ sps huangf@ujn.edu.cn

I.
INTRODUCTION


The mainstream opinion holds that the Standard Model (SM) does not contain any viable dark matter


candidate and predicts massless neutrinos 1. Currently, the cosmological and astrophysical observations


provide robust evidence for the existence of dark matter (DM)[2]. Meanwhile, the neutrino oscillation ob-


servations indicate that neutrinos have sub-eV masses[3–6]. However, the fundamental natures of DM and


neutrinos remain unclear. DM may consist of particles[7], in which the weakly interacting massive particle


(WIMP)[8, 9] and feebly interacting massive particle (FIMP)[10, 11] are the popular DM candidates. The


experiments searching for neutrinoless double-beta decay [12] do not yield a definitive signal for Majorana


neutrinos. Another alternative is Dirac neutrinos, which considerably contribute to the effective number of


relativistic neutrino species Neff via new interactions in new physics models[13–20]. The induced cosmo-


logical constraints impose stringent limits on these models incorporating dark matter[21–34].


The gauged B −L extension of the SM is a popular new physics framework [35–40], in which any


anomalies could be resolved by introducing three right-handed neutrinos νR, then producing the tiny neu-


trino masses via the seesaw mechanism [41–44]. Continuing to extend the dark sector enables connections


with DM, the cosmological observations of Neff induced by Dirac neutrinos νR could achieve the detection


of DM and the Z′ boson [45–51]. Focus on the WIMP dark matter in the resonant scenario, the minimal


extension involving only Dirac fermionic DM χ investigates the constraints from ∆Neff on the U(1)B−L


charge Qχ of DM [52]. Besides the resonance scenario [53], DM could be produced via the secluded and


FIMP scenarios [54] in this minimal U(1)B−L model, which has not been considered with Dirac neutrino


νR and viable region under ∆Neff.


The previous Planck data gives ∆Neff = Neff −NSM
eff
≲0.285 [55], where the contribution from


the SM is NSM
eff
= 3.045 [56–58]. The recent results from DESI 2024 data give a slightly weaker bound


∆Neff ≲0.4 [59], and P-ACT [60, 61] combined with Planck data pushes the bound down to ∆Neff ≲0.17


at 95% C.L.. The future CMB-S4 experiment will achieve higher sensitivity of ∆Neff ≲0.06 [62], and


CMB-HD further narrows the range to ∆Neff ≲0.027 [63]. These more stringent constraints will impose


stronger limits on the charge Qχ of DM. Thus, further investigating the impact of ∆Neff constraints on


various DM scenarios is highly valuable.


In this work, we construct the minimal U(1)B−L model that includes Dirac type right-handed neutrinos


νR and dark matter χ. Depending on the production mechanism of χ, it can be either a WIMP or a FIMP


candidate. In the WIMP scenario with resonance and secluded cases, χ has the U(1)B−L charge Qχ.


The value of |Qχ| required to reproduce the observed dark matter relic density is typically much larger


1 The recent study proposes SM neutrinos as potential dark matter candidates[1] via enhancing their density.

guishing isolated photons from light, highly boosted particles that immediately decay into

forming “photon-jets” [4–7]. Such signatures arise in SM meson decays (e.g. π0 →γγ and

of photon-jets originating from the decay of light axion-like particles (ALPs) [8–14] to two

classification of photon-jets can enhance the sensitivity to these ALP signatures, while also
improving the ability to reject π0 fakes in standard photon identification. Figure 1 provides
a schematic diagram illustrating the detector response from an EM shower resulting from

the signals in the individual cells can be leveraged directly as a high-dimensional input
modeling for a more nuanced probe of EM shower energy deposition.
The subtle correlations within an EM shower are particularly important for distin-
guishing isolated photons from light, highly boosted particles that immediately decay into
multiple photons which are so collimated they cannot be resolved as separate objects,
forming “photon-jets” [4–7]. Such signatures arise in SM meson decays (e.g. π0 →γγ and
η →γγ), and in a variety of BSM scenarios. In this study, we focus on the classification
of photon-jets originating from the decay of light axion-like particles (ALPs) [8–14] to two
photons. ALPs are a well-motivated dark matter candidate [15–22] that, for ALP masses
in the O(10–100) MeV range, can exhibit a significant branching ratio to the diphoton final
state [4, 13, 14, 23, 24]. These models often predict couplings between the ALP and the
Higgs boson or another heavy scalar mediator, leading to highly boosted ALPs which can
manifest as a photon-jet topology in the calorimeters via their γγ decays. Improving the
classification of photon-jets can enhance the sensitivity to these ALP signatures, while also
improving the ability to reject π0 fakes in standard photon identification. Figure 1 provides
a schematic diagram illustrating the detector response from an EM shower resulting from
an isolated single photon and from a photon-jet originating in an ALP decay.

Observational Details


The MACHO survey operated from 1992 to 1999, observing the Magellanic Clouds


for gravitational lensing events by Massive Compact Halo Objects - compact objects


in the galactic halo, one of the primary dark matter candidates. The programme was


undertaken from the Mount Stromlo Observatory in Australia, where the Magellanic Clouds


are circumpolar, giving brightness records free from seasonal dropouts. Information on


the equipment used in the programme can be found at http://wwwmacho.anu.edu.au/


or in [40]. 59 quasars were within the ﬁeld of view of this programme and as a result


highly sampled light curves for all of these objects were obtained.
These quasars


were observed over the duration of the programme in both V and R ﬁlters.
The


brightness records for the 59 quasars in both V and R ﬁlters are freely available at


http://www.astro.yale.edu/mgeha/MACHO/ while the entire MACHO survey data are


available from http://wwwmacho.anu.edu.au/Data/MachoData.html.


5.
Theoretical Method


Throughout this study the following assumptions were made:


1. That all autocorrelation structure on the several hundred day timescale was due to


reverberation from the Elvis outﬂows, which are also the source of the broad emission


lines in quasars. We denote the distance to this region as Rblr - the “radius of the


broad line region”.


2. That the timescale for absorption and re-emission of photons was negligable compared


to the light travel time from the central source to the outﬂow surface.


3. That the internal structure variable was less than 45o for all objects as found by [11]

I have a complete picture. The corpus was fully searched (100/100 docs, keyword mode — semantic embeddings aren't installed), and three documents mention dark matter candidates, each pointing to a different candidate class.

## Dark matter candidates in the corpus

The phrase "dark matter candidate(s)" appears in **three** of the ~100 papers, and together they name four distinct candidate classes:

**1. WIMPs and FIMPs (and the model's own particle χ)** — *"Z′ Portal Dark Matter with Observable ΔNeff"* (Liu, Han & Huang, arXiv:2607.08082)
- The paper states the Standard Model "does not contain any viable dark matter candidate," and that among particle DM, "the weakly interacting massive particle (**WIMP**)… and feebly interacting massive particle (**FIMP**)… are the popular DM candidates." (p. 2)
- Its own proposed candidate is a Dirac fermionic dark matter particle **χ** in a minimal U(1)_B−L model, which "can be either a WIMP or a FIMP candidate" depending on production mechanism (abstract p. 1; p. 2). The WIMP scenario reproduces the observed relic density via annihilation cross section ~2×10⁻²⁶ cm³/s (p. 11).
- It also notes in a footnote that "a recent study proposes **SM neutrinos** as potential dark matter candidates… via enhancing their density." (p. 2, footnote 1)

**2. Axion-like particles (ALPs)** — *"Transformer-based machine learning using low-level calorimeter signals for collimated photon identification at collider experiments"* (arXiv:2607.08175)
- "**ALPs** are a well-motivated dark matter candidate that, for ALP masses in the O(10–100) MeV range, can exhibit a significant branching ratio to the diphoton final state." (p. 3)
- The reference list corroborates this with a cited work on "**axion** dark matter detection" (p. 24, ref. [16]).

**3. MACHOs (Massive Compact Halo Objects)** — the MACHO-survey quasar reverberation paper (arXiv:0905.2570)
- The MACHO survey looked "for gravitational lensing events by **Massive Compact Halo Objects** — compact objects in the galactic halo, one of the primary dark matter candidates." (p. 12)

### Summary
| Document | Page(s) | Candidate(s) named |
|---|---|---|
| 2607.08082 — *Z′ Portal Dark Matter…* | 1, 2, 11 | WIMP, FIMP, the Dirac fermion χ, SM neutrinos |
| 2607.08175 — *Transformer-based photon ID…* | 3, 24 | Axion-like particles (ALPs) / axions |
| 0905.2570 — *MACHO-survey quasar study* | 12 | MACHOs |

Note: this was a keyword-only search (the `fastembed` package for semantic search isn't installed on this server), so it catches the literal phrase and the specific candidate terms I probed (WIMP, axion, MACHO), all of which resolved back to these same three papers. Only 2607.08082 is a dedicated dark-matter physics paper; the other two mention candidates in passing (as a detector-physics motivation, and as a definition of the survey target, respectively).
